title: Cleanup: deprecate legacy INT8 path toggle; consolidate flags and update config docs
author: Yuki Sato
release_notes: - Runtime: consolidated quantization configuration flags; legacy INT8 toggle is deprecated (warn-only) and will be removed in a future release. No default behavior change.
body: Context: As part of the FP8/INT8 benchmarking sprint we’ve accumulated multiple toggles that control INT8 enablement and selection of the INT8 execution path. This PR deprecates the legacy INT8 path toggle and consolidates quantization flags into a single, explicit configuration surface so benchmark runs and canary jobs are unambiguous and easier to attribute. Motivation: (1) avoid accidental mismatches where "INT8 enabled" still routes through a legacy path, (2) reduce combinatorial config states in perf harness + canary, (3) make kernel-selection logging and correctness guardrails easier to wire up against a single source of truth. Summary of changes: Deprecate `--runtime.enable_legacy_int8_path` (and corresponding config key) and replace with consolidated quantization settings: `--quant.mode={fp16|int8|fp8}` (default: fp16 unless model profile selects otherwise), `--quant.impl={auto|cutlass|trtllm|legacy}` (default: auto; legacy remains selectable explicitly for bisecting only), and `--quant.fallback_policy={allow|disallow}` (default: allow; emits structured event when fallback occurs). Backwards compatibility: legacy flags are still parsed but emit a startup warning and are translated into the consolidated flags following a deterministic mapping; translation is logged once at INFO. This keeps existing deploy configs and benchmark configs working while we migrate. Docs: update runtime config reference and example configs used by benchmark-lab; add a short migration snippet and explicit precedence rules. Tests: add unit tests for flag parsing/translation + precedence; add a small integration smoke test to ensure the runtime prints the deprecation warning and does not crash when the old key is present. Notes: This PR intentionally does not remove the legacy kernel implementation; it only makes it opt-in behind `--quant.impl=legacy` for controlled experiments. Follow-up: remove the deprecated flag in ~2 release trains after benchmark-lab configs and canary jobs are updated everywhere (tracked in ENG-24810).
commits: runtime/config: introduce QuantConfig (mode/impl/fallback) and wire to startup config
runtime/config: parse legacy INT8 flags and translate; emit deprecation warning
runtime/docs: update config reference + examples; add migration notes
tests: add config precedence + translation unit tests
benchmark presets: update sample configs to use quant.mode/quant.impl
conversation: Grace Kim (review): Can we confirm the precedence rules are explicit? Right now it looks like `quant.mode` wins, but if someone sets `enable_int8=true` + `quant.mode=fp16` I want the behavior to be deterministic (and ideally noisy).

Yuki Sato (author): Yes — added a precedence table in docs and a unit test. `quant.mode` is the single source of truth; legacy keys are translated only if `quant.mode` is unset. If both are present we keep `quant.mode` and emit a WARNING listing ignored legacy keys.
Noah Patel (review): Please make sure we don’t accidentally change defaults for hosted. Are any model profiles relying on the legacy toggle being on by default somewhere?

Yuki Sato (author): No default flips in this PR. `quant.mode` defaults to fp16 at runtime-config level; model registry overrides are applied downstream exactly as before. I also added a startup log line that prints the resolved quant config (mode/impl/fallback_policy) to make this visible in perf runs.
Connor O'Brien (review): For release train: can we keep the old flag working for at least 2 releases? Also please add a release note blurb and a linkable warning string for support to grep.

Yuki Sato (author): Done. Deprecation warning includes a stable token `DEPRECATED_QUANT_FLAG_LEGACY_INT8` and the release note is added. Removal will be handled in a later PR once benchmark configs and canary jobs are migrated.
Sahana Iyer (review): CI: the integration test should assert the warning is emitted once (not per worker). Can you make the emission happen in the primary process only?

Yuki Sato (author): Updated emission to be once per runtime init (before worker fork), and the test now checks a single occurrence. Also added a guard to prevent duplicate warnings if config is reloaded.
CI (bot): build-linux-gpu failed: tools/config-linter (rule violation: legacy flag in example configs).
Yuki Sato (author): Fixed by updating remaining example configs + adding linter allowlist for testdata only. Re-running CI.
CI (bot): All checks passed (build-linux-gpu, unit, lint, docs, integration-smoke).
Noah Patel (review): Approved — thanks for tightening the surface area; will help attribute perf deltas.
